source_text: Postquam enim dixerat: In omnes homines pertransiit, subdidit statim: in quo omnes peccaverunt; hoc: in quo omnes peccaverunt, nihil aliud indicat quam: Quia omnes peccaverunt secundum illud Davidicum: In quo corrigit adulescentior viam suam? Id est: Quomodo corrigit viam suam? In custodiendo sermones tuos [n276] . Io eo ergo corrigi dicitur, per quod et corrigitur. Ita et Apostolus in eo dixit pertransisse mortem, in quo omnes propria voluntate peccaverunt, non ut hoc: in quo aut Adam aut peccatum videatur ostendere, sed in quo omnes peccantes intellegatur exprimere.
pass_a_gloss: For after he had said: It passed through into all human beings, he subjoined at once: in whom all sinned; this: in whom all sinned, indicates nothing other than: Because all sinned according to that of David: In what does a younger one correct his way? That is: How does he correct his way? In guarding your speeches. In that therefore he is said to be corrected, through which he is also corrected. So also the Apostle said that death passed through in that in which all sinned by their own will, not so that this: in whom may seem to show either Adam or sin, but in whom may be understood to express all sinning.

pass_b_english: For after saying, ‘It passed into all human beings,’ he immediately added, ‘in whom all sinned’ (Romans 5:12). This phrase, ‘in whom all sinned,’ indicates nothing other than ‘because all sinned,’ in accordance with David’s words: ‘In what does a young man correct his way?’ (Psalm 119:9;) That is, ‘How does he correct his way?’ ‘By keeping your words’ (Psalm 119:9; LXX/Vulgate 118:9). He is thus said to be corrected ‘in’ that through which he is corrected. Likewise, the apostle said death passed on ‘in’ the fact that all sinned by their own will. The phrase ‘in whom’ should not be taken to indicate either Adam or sin; it should be understood as expressing the fact that all sinned.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: Julian’s argument turns on the Latin in quo, which he takes causally (“because”), rather than as referring to Adam (“in whom”). The English keeps both readings visible so his grammatical argument can be followed.
